body.p: The Oxygen AI Positron exposes a hook system that lets developers intercept events fired during the AI lifecycle. A hook handler can observe fire-and-forget events for auditing or analytics, or veto blocking events to prevent an action from running.

ul.li: Auditing every AI action, tool call, or shell command to an external log or compliance system.
Gating risky operations (for example, blocking shell commands that modify production files).
Controlling sub-agent execution to enforce organizational policies on autonomous AI tasks.
Collecting token usage metrics after each assistant turn.

section.title: Implementing a Hook Handler
section.p: You can use the sample plugin available on GitHub as a reference when building your own hook handler: .

section.title: Hook Events Reference
section.p: The following tables list all events defined in AIHookEvent, grouped by lifecycle category. Events marked as Blocking can be vetoed by throwing an AIHookVetoException inside eventOccurred. Events marked as Fire-and-forget are informational (throwing an exception has no effect on the AI action).

Every event delivers its data as a JSON string (payloadJson) with snake_case keys. Deserialize it with Jackson into the event-specific BaseHookPayload subclass (listed under each event below) to access its fields. All payload types share the following base fields:

strow.stentry: Stable identifier for the current chat session, constant across all turns.
Identifier of the AI action or agent (chat mode) that produced this event (e.g. agent, ask, or a custom chat mode ID).
Identifier that changes with each user message/AI generation round.
Identifier of the AI connection as configured by the user in Preferences.
The AI model currently in use (e.g. claude-opus-4-7).
The name of the hook event that fired (e.g. beforeShellExecution).
Running version of the AI Positron plugin (e.g. 8.3.0).
Running version of the host application (e.g. 27.1.0).
Host product distribution (e.g. Oxygen XML Editor).
Absolute path to the current project or workspace root.

dlentry.dd: Fired when a new AI session is created. This includes interactive chat conversations, batch AI refactoring sessions, and AI XPath function invocations.

strow.stentry: Human-readable name of the AI action that started the session.

Classifies the kind of session: chat for an interactive chat conversation, refactoring for a batch AI refactoring run, or xpath_function for an AI invocation triggered from an XPath extension function.

dlentry.dd: Fired when an AI session ends, whether a chat conversation is closed or cleared, a batch AI refactoring run finishes, or an AI XPath function invocation completes.

strow.stentry: Reason the session ended: user_close (the user manually closed or cleared the chat), application_close (the host application is shutting down), completed (the session completed normally, for example, a refactoring batch run or an AI XPath function invocation finished successfully), aborted (the user pressed Stop during an invocation before it finished), or error (the invocation was terminated by an unexpected error).
Classifies the kind of session that ended: chat, refactoring, or xpath_function. Matches the value emitted in the corresponding sessionStart event.

dlentry.dd: Fired when the user restores a previous conversation from the chat history.

strow.stentry: Human-readable name of the AI action that was active when this session was originally created.
Classifies the kind of session being reloaded: chat or refactoring.

dlentry.dd: Fired before an AI action is launched. Throwing an exception vetoes the action and prevents it from running. The action identifier is available via the base field action_or_agent_id.

strow.stentry: The text content of the initial user input passed to the action.

URL of the document targeted by the action. Set when the action operates on a specific document, either an open editor (replace, insert, or analyze actions) or a file processed during an AI batch refactoring job. Absent when the action has no single document target (for example, new-document or prompt-user actions).
URLs of attachments included in the initial user input. Omitted when empty.
IDs of the tools available to the model for this request. Omitted when empty.
Expanded runtime parameters used to invoke the action (key-value pairs). Omitted when empty.

dlentry.dd: Fired right before a user prompt is submitted to the AI model from the chat UI. Throwing an exception prevents the prompt from being sent.

strow.stentry: The full text of the prompt the user is about to submit.
URLs of attachments included by user. Omitted when empty.
IDs of the tools available to the model for this request. Omitted when empty.
Expanded runtime parameters used to invoke the action (key-value pairs). Omitted when empty.
URL of the document currently open in the editor when the prompt is submitted. Absent when no document is open.

dlentry.dd: Fired when the AI agent interaction finishes, regardless of whether it completed successfully, was aborted by the user, or terminated by an error.

strow.stentry: Reason the interaction ended: completed, aborted, or error.
Number of tool-call rounds completed during the interaction (0 for plain Q&A with no tools).
Human-readable error description. Present only when status is error.

dlentry.dd: Fired before any AI tool (function or action) is invoked. Throwing an exception prevents the tool from running.

strow.stentry: ID of the tool about to be invoked (e.g. invoke_cmd_line).
Tool arguments as a raw JSON object.
Unique identifier for this specific tool call, assigned by the AI model.

dlentry.dd: Fired after a tool has completed successfully. Use it for auditing, analytics, or collecting tool execution metrics.

strow.stentry: Name of the tool that was invoked.
Tool arguments as a raw JSON object.
Output produced by the tool execution.
Unique identifier for this specific tool call, assigned by the AI model.

dlentry.dd: Fired after a tool invocation has failed, timed out, or was denied.

strow.stentry: Name of the tool that failed.
Tool arguments as a raw JSON object.
Unique identifier for this specific tool call, assigned by the AI model.

dlentry.dd: Fired before a sub-agent or sub-action is started. Throwing an exception prevents the sub-agent from being created.

strow.stentry: Identifier of the sub-action or sub-agent being started (e.g. improve-readability).
Human-readable name of the sub-action or sub-agent.
The document content or text fragment that the sub-agent will process.
Session ID of the parent agent that spawned this sub-agent.

dlentry.dd: Fired when a sub-agent finishes, errors, or is abandoned.

strow.stentry: Identifier of the sub-action or sub-agent that ended.
Outcome of the sub-agent: completed or failed.
Total wall-clock duration of the sub-agent execution in milliseconds.

dlentry.dd: Fired before a shell command is executed by the AI agent. Throwing an exception prevents the command from running. This is the primary hook to use when enforcing shell command policies.

strow.stentry: The full shell command string about to be executed.
Maximum allowed execution time in seconds. Absent if no limit is set.

dlentry.dd: Fired after a shell command has finished executing. Use it for auditing or collecting metrics from command output.

strow.stentry: The shell command that was executed.
Combined stdout/stderr output of the command.
Process exit code, or absent if the process was terminated abnormally.
Wall-clock duration of the command execution in milliseconds.
true if the command ran without a system-level error, regardless of the process exit code; false if execution failed before the process could complete (e.g. IOException, unsupported platform).

dlentry.dd: Fired before an MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool is invoked. Throwing an exception prevents the tool from running.

strow.stentry: Name of the MCP server hosting the tool.
Name of the MCP tool to be invoked.
Tool arguments as a raw JSON object.

dlentry.dd: Fired after an MCP tool execution completes, whether successfully or with an error. Includes the tool's input parameters, the JSON result, and the execution outcome.

strow.stentry: Name of the MCP server that hosted the tool.
Name of the MCP tool that was invoked.
Tool arguments as a raw JSON object.
Result returned by the MCP tool as a raw JSON value. Absent when the execution failed.
true if the MCP tool completed successfully; false if it threw an error.
Human-readable description of the failure. Absent when succeeded is true.

dlentry.dd: Fired before the agent reads a file. Throwing an exception blocks the agent's access to that file. Use this hook to implement file-level access control (for example, to prevent the AI from reading files that contain secrets). Also fired before the agent reads the DITA map structure context (the Get DITA Map Structure Context tool), with file_path set to the URL of the DITA map currently open in the DITA Maps Manager.

strow.stentry: Absolute path or URL of the file about to be read.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the agent successfully reads a file. Use it to audit file-access patterns or log the content retrieved by the agent. Also fired after the Get DITA Map Structure Context tool completes successfully, with content set to the computed hierarchy JSON (not the raw DITA map XML).

strow.stentry: Absolute path or URL of the file that was read.
The content that was read from the file. For the Get DITA Map Structure Context tool, this is the computed hierarchy JSON returned to the AI model, not the raw DITA map XML.

dlentry.dd: Fired before the agent edits or creates a file. Throwing an exception prevents the write from happening (the exception message is returned to the AI model as an error).The event is fired only when the content to be written has been successfully computed. For replacement-based edits, this means the replacement strings were located in the existing file content. This event is also fired for DITA map structure additions (inserting a topic reference via the Add to DITA Map Structure tool).

strow.stentry: Absolute path or URL of the file about to be modified or created.
Type of operation about to be performed: create or edit.
The full content that will be written to the file. null for DITA map structure additions, where the final content is computed internally by the Author API and is not available before the write.

The individual text replacements about to be applied. Each fragment contains an old_value and a new_value. Absent when the entire file content will be written at once. For DITA map structure additions, a single fragment is provided with old_value set to an empty string and new_value set to the topicref element about to be inserted (e.g. <topicref href='topic.dita'/>).

dlentry.dd: Fired after the agent attempts to edit or create a file, both on success and on failure. Also fired after a DITA map structure addition (inserting a topic reference). Use it to audit AI-generated file changes.

strow.stentry: Absolute path or URL of the file that was modified or created.
Type of operation performed: create or edit.
The complete file content after a successful write, or null when the write failed. For fragment-based edits, this is the full document with all replacements already merged in.
The result string returned to the AI model after the tool call completed (e.g. a success confirmation or an error message).
true when the file was written to disk successfully, false when the save failed.

dlentry.dd: Fired before the agent loads a skill by name. Throwing an exception prevents the skill from being loaded.

strow.stentry: The name of the skill about to be loaded.
The URL or path of the skill file. Absent when the skill location cannot be resolved before loading.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the agent successfully loads a skill. Use it to audit which skills are used during an AI session.

strow.stentry: The name of the skill that was loaded.
The URL or path of the skill file. Absent when the skill location cannot be resolved.
The full content of the skill that was loaded.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the agent completes an assistant turn, whether the turn contained only tool calls or produced a visible text response.

strow.stentry: The text content of the completed assistant turn. Empty string when the turn consisted solely of tool calls.
Names of the tools called in this turn. Omitted when empty.
Token usage information for this assistant turn. Contains prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and total_tokens. Omitted when not reported by the backend.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the agent completes a thinking block (extended thinking mode). Use it to observe the agent's reasoning process.

strow.stentry: The thinking/reasoning text. Depending on the model, it may be a summary or the complete text.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the user clicks the Insert/Replace button in the chat panel to apply an AI suggestion in the document.

strow.stentry: The content that was inserted or used to replace the selection.
URL of the editor (document) where the content was inserted. Absent if the target editor could not be determined.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the user clicks the Preview button in the chat panel and the preview dialog box closes. The preview opens a diff view comparing the current editor content with the result of applying the AI response, so the user can review the changes before deciding whether to apply them.

strow.stentry: The content that was sent to the preview dialog box.
true if the user applied the changes from within the preview dialog box, false if the dialog box was closed without applying.
URL of the editor (document) where the preview was shown. Absent if the target editor could not be determined.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the user clicks the Copy button in the chat panel to copy an AI response to the clipboard.

strow.stentry: The text that was copied to the system clipboard.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the user accepts AI-proposed file changes. This event is emitted both when the user accepts changes from the agentic chat flow and when the user accepts files in the batch AI refactoring diff dialog.

strow.stentry: List of absolute paths or URLs of the documents whose changes were accepted.

dlentry.dd: Fired after the user rejects AI-proposed file changes. This event is emitted both when the user rejects changes from the agentic chat flow and when files are rejected in the batch AI refactoring diff dialog (including when the dialog is cancelled, in which case all files in the batch are treated as rejected).

strow.stentry: List of absolute paths or URLs of the documents whose changes were rejected.

body.note: The AIHooksHandler extension point is available starting with version 28.0 of .
